scenes.heading: Gradient
scenes.sub: One number that tells you how steep
scenes.say: How steep is that hill, that roof, or that line on a graph? One number answers all three: the gradient.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A hill: how much you climb for each step forward
scenes.science: Gradient: how much y rises for each 1 across
scenes.breaks: On a hill you can walk either way. On a graph you always read left to right, so downhill is negative.
scenes.say: Walk up a hill. Climb one metre for every ten forward and it's gentle. Climb five metres for every ten and you're puffing. Steepness compares the climb with the distance forward. On a graph we always read left to right, so going downhill gives a negative gradient.

scenes.heading: Rise over run
parts: change in y (up is +, down is −)
scenes.say: Gradient equals rise divided by run. The rise is the change in y: up is positive, down is negative. The run is the change in x, going to the right. Remember: you rise before you run.

scenes.heading: Rise and run on a graph
scenes.say: Here is a line through two, three and five, nine. First the run: three squares across to the right. Then the rise: six squares up. Rise over run is six divided by three, so the gradient is two.
scenes.caption: From (2, 3) to (5, 9): run 3, rise 6, so gradient = 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

scenes.heading: Four kinds of line
scenes.say: Reading left to right, an uphill line has a positive gradient and a downhill line has a negative gradient. A flat line has gradient zero. A vertical line has a run of zero, and you can't divide by zero, so its gradient is undefined.

scenes.heading: Gradient from two points
scenes.question: Find the gradient of the line through (−2, 5) and (2, −3).
scenes.say: Find the gradient through negative two, five and two, negative three. The rise is negative three minus five, which is negative eight. The run is two minus negative two, which is four. Negative eight divided by four is negative two. The line goes downhill, so negative makes sense.
scenes.caption: Find the gradient through (−2, 5) and (2, −3). Rise = −3 − 5 = −8. Run = 2 − (−2) = 4. −8 ÷ 4 = −2. The line goes downhill, so negative makes sense.

scenes.heading: Which is steeper?
scenes.say: Is a gradient of negative three less steep than two? No! Steepness is the size of the number, ignoring the sign. Negative three goes down three for every one across, so it's steeper than a line going up two.

scenes.heading: A negative rise
scenes.say: Here is that example drawn. From negative two, five, run four to the right, then the rise goes down eight, so it is negative eight. Negative eight over four is negative two.
scenes.caption: Run 4 to the right, then down 8: rise −8. Gradient = −8 ÷ 4 = −2.

points: Read left to right: up +, down −
Same order on top and bottom
scenes.say: Quick recap. Gradient is rise over run. Read left to right: uphill is positive, downhill is negative. Flat is zero, vertical is undefined. And subtract in the same order on top and bottom. Now try the practice questions!
